questions.cardText:
[History] What does the term “chai” mean in chai latte?
A. Tea B. Spice C. Milk
Answer: A. Tea was one of the most exported items from China to the world in ancient times. In countries where tea was brought overland, it’s often called “chai,” reflecting the northern Mandarin pronunciation “cha.” In contrast, in places where it was transported by sea, like Europe, it’s called “tea,” reflecting the pronunciation “te” from the Southern Min dialect.
questions.de: Was bedeutet das Wort „Chai“ wie in Chai Latte?
questions.en: What does the word “chai”, as in chai latte, mean?

timeline.labelEn: The word 'chai' enters English, via Russian or Arabic, in the early 20th century
timeline.labelDe: Das Wort „chai“ gelangt im frühen 20. Jahrhundert über das Russische oder Arabische ins Englische

questions.notes: Wikipedia: chai came overland via the Silk Road, picking up a Persian ending, possibly from the northern Chinese pronunciation chá; 'tea' from Min tê via sea trade. Card fine. Answer may also be phrased 'tea (from Persian chāy, from Chinese chá)'.

questions.cardText:
[Art History] The “Mona Lisa” became extremely famous largely after:
A. Leonardo da Vinci declared it his finest work
B. It was stolen from the Louvre in 1911
C. Its subject’s identity was revealed
Answer: B.
questions.de: Welches Ereignis des Jahres 1911 machte Leonardos Mona Lisa zu einem der bekanntesten Gemälde der Welt?
questions.en: What event of 1911 turned Leonardo's Mona Lisa into one of the best-known paintings in the world?
questions.answerDe: Ihr Diebstahl aus dem Louvre (durch Vincenzo Peruggia)
questions.answerEn: Its theft from the Louvre (by Vincenzo Peruggia)

timeline.labelEn: The Mona Lisa is stolen from the Louvre by Vincenzo Peruggia
timeline.labelDe: Die Mona Lisa wird von Vincenzo Peruggia aus dem Louvre gestohlen

questions.notes: The painting was already famous; the theft's headlines and police hunt made it one of the best known in the world (Wikipedia). Returned to the Louvre in 1913.
